name: deinterleave_four_bitplanes
description: Copies 4000 words from a source table, splitting each group of four consecutive words across four destination arrays at fixed offsets from the destination pointer. The loop runs until its counter wraps past zero.

name: deinterleave_four_bitplanes
description: Single-instruction entry whose decompiled body is the same four-way word copy loop as the neighbouring routine, so it appears to be a duplicate of that code rather than separate behaviour.

name: deinterleave_four_bitplanes
description: Entered through a block-move instruction, its decompiled body is the same four-way word copy loop that splits 4000 source words into four destination arrays, one word per array per step.

name: interleave_planes_with_zero_padding
description: Expands source groups of eight words into four planes that sit 48 words apart, writing two data words per plane and zeroing the third word of each group. The outer loop repeats for a block count supplied by the caller.

name: clear_state_block_and_load_tables
description: When a guard pointer is set, clears a 256-byte state area, copies three four-byte values from a lookup table selected by a flag, sets several state bytes to fixed constants and returns 1. The listing also records interrupt-enable register writes that the pseudo-code does not show directly.

name: reset_state_block_from_tables
description: When a guard pointer is set, clears a 256-byte state area, loads four-byte table values selected by a flag and sets several state bytes to fixed constants. The listing records interrupt-enable register writes that the pseudo-code does not show directly.

name: reset_mode_and_invoke_handler
description: Returns immediately unless a guard pointer is set; otherwise sets a control byte to a fixed value, clears a mode word and calls one subroutine.

name: stub_empty_return_routine
description: Contains only a return with no work. It is reached only because the gap between routines decodes as code.

name: run_four_handler_passes
description: When a guard is set, combines and tests a counter value, then either calls a handler four times or stores a fallback value, calls the handler once more and returns. It finishes by setting a control byte to a fixed high value.

name: call_handler_four_times
description: When a guard pointer is set, calls a handler routine exactly four times in a loop.

name: load_channel_pointer_when_flagged
description: If a per-channel flag byte is set, clears it, looks up a buffer pointer in a table indexed by channel number, and stores that pointer and its first word into two destinations. The listing records DMA control register writes that the pseudo-code does not show directly.

name: store_channel_buffer_pointer
description: Loads a buffer pointer from a structure and stores a pointer to a point further into the same buffer, along with the buffer's first word, into two destinations. It also copies a word from a table and sets a flag byte when a bit is set in the source.

name: reset_object_pattern_fields
description: When a counter is below four, copies one state byte to another, clears another, and writes two fixed four-byte patterns and several zero longwords into an object.

name: write_word_via_pointer
description: Writes the input word through a pointer computed from a base address and an offset.

name: update_clamped_value
description: Takes a byte and reduces it to a quarter of a global value when that is smaller. When a mode value equals 13 and a per-object byte is nonzero, it sets the result to one more than that byte, then stores the result as a word.

name: decrement_and_update_state
description: Returns early unless a flag byte is negative. Otherwise it steps several per-object countdown counters, toggles a phase byte, advances a value by a table-driven delta and calls helper routines. The decompiled listing is incomplete, so the end of the routine is not fully recovered.

name: clear_piece_state
description: Copies one state byte to another, clears a second state byte and sets a third to seven. It then writes two fixed four-byte patterns and six zero longwords into an object.

name: store_values_then_adjust_counter
description: Writes two table values into fixed memory cells, calls a helper routine, and if the helper's result is negative adds a fixed offset to a global value.

name: store_default_parameter_block
description: Writes nine fixed starting values into nine global variables: zero, 980, 79, 40, two minus-one sentinels, two zeros and one.

name: loop_steps_until_countdown_ends
description: Sets a counter to three and clears a flag, then repeatedly runs a sequence of helper calls. It stops when a helper returns a negative value, when a second helper result is non-negative while the flag is zero, or when the counter reaches zero.

name: copy_table_entries_four_passes
description: Runs four passes over a table of entries that ends in minus one. For each entry it calls helper routines and, unless a status flag is set, copies a run of bytes from a source record into a destination buffer, sized by a count field.

name: verify_table_checksum
description: Sums 128 longwords from a fixed table, subtracting each one, and returns zero if the total equals a stored reference value or minus one otherwise.

name: copy_nonzero_entries_until_end
description: Calls a helper, then copies the nonzero longwords of a record's table into an output list in reverse order, repeating while a chained link value stays nonzero. It finishes by writing a minus-one terminator.

name: find_matching_table_record
description: Scans a table of fixed-size records, comparing each record's name bytes against a reference buffer. On a match it stores the record's first word and the following longword and returns zero; if no record matches it returns minus one.

name: populate_record_list_from_table
description: Once only, walks a word table ending in minus one and calls a helper for each entry. It writes a record holding the result, a longword, 29 bytes copied from a fixed source and a minus-one terminator, stops early if a status flag is raised, then sets a done flag.

name: fill_record_list_from_word_table
description: Once only, walks a word table ending in minus one, calling a helper for each entry and writing a record with the result, a longword, 29 bytes from a fixed source and a terminator. It stops early when a status flag is raised, then sets a done flag. Its body matches the neighbouring record-filling routine, with extra helper calls.

name: copy_nonzero_words_into_list
description: Once only, walks a source table of words, copying each nonzero word into an output list, skipping zeros, and ends the list with minus one.

name: copy_longword_block_when_clear
description: When not already done and the status check from a helper passes, copies 128 longwords from a source pointer to a destination pointer.

name: copy_longword_block_after_check
description: When not already done and a helper's status check passes, copies 128 longwords from one pointer to another. It is the same block copy as the neighbouring routine, reached through a different entry.

name: update_global_status
description: Calls a helper and stores its result in a status global. If that result is non-negative, it calls two more helpers and stores the second helper's nonzero result in the status global.

name: split_value_by_22_into_fields
description: Stores the input word, divides the input value by 22 into a quotient and a remainder, and stores both. If the remainder exceeds ten it subtracts 11 from it and sets a flag recording that the subtraction happened.

name: split_value_by_22_into_fields
description: Same code as the neighbouring routine: stores the input word, splits the input value by 22 into a quotient and remainder, and sets a flag when the remainder exceeded ten.

name: program_disk_read_registers
description: Programs the disk controller for a read. It writes a disk pointer, a sync word and a control value, sets the disk length register to a fixed transfer value, enables disk DMA, and stores a fixed status value in a global. The listing records the disk register writes.

name: poll_disk_transfer_completion
description: Repeats while two stored positions differ. Each pass records the new positions, writes a fixed transfer length twice and polls a status bit for up to 65,535 iterations. It returns zero as soon as the bit is seen; otherwise, once the positions match, it returns the result of a final helper.

name: call_two_helpers_in_sequence
description: Calls two helper routines one after the other and returns, with no other logic.

name: scan_table_until_routine_succeeds
description: Repeatedly finds the next record in a fixed table whose first word matches a counter, calls a routine with it, and increments the counter. It stops when that routine returns one and then returns zero.

name: interleave_bits_of_paired_longs
description: Reads 128 longwords from a source table and merges each one with the longword 128 entries ahead, interleaving their even and odd bits into a destination table of 128 longwords.

name: pack_bit_interleave_table_entries
description: Calls a helper, then for each of eleven entries interleaves the bits of two longword fields and writes the high and low bytes of the low word into a table, advancing 16 bytes per entry.

name: locate_sync_words_in_buffer
description: Stores a fixed buffer address as the first entry, then scans a data buffer for a sync word and records up to ten match positions in a table. It backs up one word when the word after a match is not the sync word, and stops at the end of the buffer.

name: step_position_toward_target
description: Returns minus one when the current value is 79 or more. Otherwise it steps a stored position one step at a time toward a target value, calling two helpers per step, then stores the final position, calls one more helper and returns zero.

name: repeat_helpers_until_flag_clears
description: When two stored values differ, repeatedly calls two helper routines while a status bit stays set, then clears a counter. The listing records a touch of the joystick and disk status register, which the pseudo-code does not show directly.

name: busy_wait_countdown
description: Spins by decrementing a register until it reaches zero, then returns. It is a pure delay loop with no other effect.

name: mask_control_port_bit
description: Takes an input byte, clears one bit chosen by a stored index, combines the result with a fixed mask and stores it in a global variable. The listing records a touch of the second CIA port B register.

name: write_control_byte_until_ready
description: Builds a control byte by clearing one bit chosen by a stored index, then sets or clears bit two depending on a flag. It stores that byte in a global and repeats the write until bit five reads clear. The listing records touches of both CIA port registers.

name: clear_control_bit_then_delay
description: Clears one control bit chosen by a stored index, waits while bit five stays set, then runs a fixed countdown delay.

name: access_cia_port_b
description: An eight-instruction routine that touches the second CIA port B register. The decompiler timed out, so only the listing facts are available and the exact operation cannot be confirmed from the evidence.

name: initialise_state_and_run_setup
description: Clears and sets initial globals and a flag, then makes a long series of helper calls, each preceded by writing a fixed parameter block into a global record. It finishes with calls to two more helpers. It is the entry sequence of the raw code region.

name: run_update_sequence_until_done
description: Repeats a sequence of helper calls, clearing a flag byte when it is set and waiting until a global reaches three, until a counter reaches a value from a table. It then calls a helper and keeps calling another until its result is zero.

name: run_twelve_step_update_cycle
description: Runs a fixed sequence of seven helper calls on each pass of a counter that goes from twelve down through zero, so thirteen passes in total.

name: run_twelve_step_update_cycle
